node_definition.done_when:
ONE TEST BLOCKS AN ENTIRE RELEASE CHAIN. Read tests/test_physical_base_kinds.py in full - it is under 40 lines - and nothing else beyond the vocabulary loader it calls.

THE FAILURE, from continuous integration on the open upstream pull request. build (3.12), build (3.13) and coverage all fail on test_only_momentum_and_torque_bases_change_to_vector at tests/test_physical_base_kinds.py:29, with a digest mismatch: expected 6062e5c22be7788220b390f09a5c8c1f1037ece0f8bc4422b2e6a3e3b1763956, observed 7df8c3f2f3a6ed41ce28fdbb49b0bb4045b8717966a4999244433afaf579e3c4. The fast build job passes; only the test jobs fail.

WHY IT MOVED, and it is not a regression. _kind_map_digest hashes every name=kind pair returned by load_physical_bases().bases except the three names in _VECTOR_CORRECTIONS, and _BASELINE_UNCHANGED_KIND_DIGEST is frozen as a module literal. Thirty-one vocabulary tokens were deliberately added on this branch - twenty-five bare tokens and six data-dictionary-backed ones - and the beta inclination qualifier was withdrawn. So the digest moved because the vocabulary grew, not because any existing base changed kind.

THE DECISION IS ALREADY LOCKED in the plan, decision key kind-pin-shape: pin each baseline base's kind BY NAME, and do not simply refresh the frozen digest. Refreshing restores the suite and leaves the defect, so the next vocabulary addition breaks it again.

READ THE THIRD ASSERTION BEFORE YOU CHANGE ANYTHING, because it changes what you must preserve. The test makes three claims. The first, that the three named corrections carry kind vector, is real. The third builds baseline_kinds from the CURRENT kind map by overriding those same three entries to scalar, then asserts exactly those three differ - which, given the first assertion, is true by construction and can never fail. Verify that reading yourself and state your conclusion. If you agree it is vacuous, replace it rather than preserving it; if you find a case where it can fail, say what that case is and keep it. Do not delete an assertion you have not shown to be empty.

THE DELIVERABLE: an assertion that fails when an existing base's kind changes and passes when a new base is added. Record the baseline as an explicit name-to-kind mapping for the bases that exist now, compare only those keys, and let unlisted names through. Keep the first assertion exactly as it is. The test's name promises that only momentum and torque bases became vector, so also assert that NO base outside _VECTOR_CORRECTIONS carries kind vector - that is the claim the name makes and the frozen digest only approximated.

PROVE BOTH DIRECTIONS, and this is the measure. Show the suite passing at the current vocabulary. Then show the new assertion FAILING when an existing base's kind is altered - do that by mutating the loaded mapping inside a test, never by editing a vocabulary file - and show it PASSING when a synthetic new base is added to the loaded mapping. A gate that only demonstrates the green case has not been shown to catch anything.

Run once before your change and once after:
uv run pytest tests/test_physical_base_kinds.py -p no:cacheprovider
Then run the whole grammar suite once after your change as a blast-radius check and report its counts: uv run pytest tests/ -p no:cacheprovider
Report the before and after counts for both. The baseline mapping must be MEASURED from the loader, never transcribed from anything I have told you.

CONSTRAINTS. Change no vocabulary file, no parser, no renderer - this node touches the test module only. Do not edit the digest helper into something that still hashes a growing map. Do not add a date, a version, a plan name or a pull-request number anywhere in the module. This repository's environment is its own, so plain uv run is correct here.

OPERATIONAL RECEIPT REQUIRED IN YOUR MANIFEST: your wall-clock from first tool call to manifest write, your number of tool calls, how many turns you used, whether any request was retried or refused and why, and one sentence naming what you had to discover versus what this brief handed you, including anything under-specified.

node_definition.done_when:
A CLASSIFICATION DEFECT IN THE PARSER, NOT A PLACEMENT RULE. The lead has specified the correct behaviour and the evidence localises the cause. Do not change the tail-relocation rule; it is not implicated.

THE EVIDENCE, measured against the live grammar. These three spellings all parse to an IDENTICAL intermediate representation:
  toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_lithium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
  flux_surface_averaged_toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
  toroidal_lithium_velocity_flux_surface_averaged_at_plasma_boundary
and that representation is:
  operators: []
  projection: {axis: toroidal, shape: component}
  qualifiers: [{token: flux_surface_averaged}, {token: lithium}]
  base: {token: velocity, kind: quantity}
  locus: {relation: at, token: plasma_boundary, type: position}

So `flux_surface_averaged` is landing in QUALIFIERS with an empty operators list. Contrast the untailed, unprojected control `flux_surface_averaged_magnetic_field_magnitude`, which parses correctly with operators carrying an OperatorApplication for flux_surface_averaged with bare_prefix true, alongside the magnitude postfix. Same token, two classifications, and the difference is the presence of a projection or a locus tail.

THE CONSEQUENCE, and it is why this blocks a release rather than being cosmetic. A trailing qualifier renders after the projection and base and before the tail, which is why the composer emits toroidal_lithium_velocity_flux_surface_averaged_at_plasma_boundary. And because the token sits in qualifiers rather than operators, the representation cannot distinguish a flux-surface-averaged quantity from an unaveraged one carrying a stray qualifier - representation equality is this project's test for meaning equality, and a downstream consumer uses exactly that test to decide whether a rename preserves meaning.

THE REQUIRED BEHAVIOUR, from the lead verbatim: the flux-surface-average operator is ALWAYS FIRST - flux surface average OF the quantity. It wraps everything including the projection. So the canonical spelling for that representation is:
  flux_surface_averaged_toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
The authored spelling was also wrong, for the opposite reason: it placed the projection OUTSIDE the operator. Neither the authored form nor the current canonical form is correct, so the target is a third spelling.

WHERE TO LOOK FIRST, before changing anything. The operator is registered as kind unary_prefix, precedence 30, with flux_surface_reduction true, and it renders joiner-free through a bare_prefix path at grammar/render.py:196. A helper at grammar/render.py:302 named _leading_bare_operators exists to split leading bare operators from ordinary base qualifiers and is called at :341 - which is machinery built for exactly this, and it is not producing the leading form here. Establish whether the defect is that the PARSER never classifies the token as an operator when a projection or locus is present, or that it does classify it and the renderer's split fails to lead with it. Report which, with the file and line that decides it. The fix belongs wherever that answer points, and I do not want a compensating change at the other end.

PRESERVE THE REDUCTION CLASS CONSISTENTLY. volume_averaged, line_integrated and root_mean_square share kind unary_prefix at precedence 30; flux_surface_averaged additionally carries flux_surface_reduction. Say whether your fix generalises to all operators at that precedence or is specific to the flux-surface reduction, and prefer the general form if the evidence supports it. Note also an existing inconsistency worth reporting but NOT fixing here: gyroaveraged is registered unary_postfix at precedence 10 while its semantic siblings are prefix at 30.

WHAT MUST NOT MOVE. A downstream consumer measured 2,339 of 2,347 accepted names rendering byte-identical under the current grammar. Your change must not disturb that. The untailed control flux_surface_averaged_magnetic_field_magnitude must stay byte-identical, and so must the recursive control flux_surface_averaged_ratio_of_square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude_to_square_of_major_radius.

EVIDENCE REQUIRED. Add tests pinning: the representation for the tailed projected name now carrying flux_surface_averaged in operators rather than qualifiers; the canonical spelling being flux_surface_averaged_toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary; a strict parse of that spelling succeeding and round-tripping; a strict parse of both wrong spellings being rejected as non-canonical while still parsing to the same representation; and both controls byte-identical. Run once before your change and once after:
  uv run pytest tests/ -p no:cacheprovider
Report both full-suite counts. The suite is the blast radius and it must not lose a passing test; if it does, name each loss and stop rather than adjusting expectations.

Do not touch the vocabulary's precedence numbers unless your diagnosis shows precedence is the cause, and say so explicitly if it is. This repository's environment is its own, so plain uv run is correct.

OPERATIONAL RECEIPT IN YOUR MANIFEST: wall clock from first tool call to manifest write, tool calls, turns used, any request retried or refused and why, and one sentence naming what you had to discover versus what this brief handed you.
